clue.text: Something in the coat line that's groovy

definitions.note: a phrase standing for 'something with a groove in it', a noun

parts.note: fur is what lines or trims a winter coat
a row is a line of things side by side

explanation.surface: A furrier admires a smart stripe running along a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groovy' is the 1960s slang for fashionable, but here it means literally having a groove; 'that's groovy' stands for a thing that is a groove.
explanation.definitionFit: A furrow is a long narrow trench cut in the ground, a groove in a field or a brow.

clue.text: But not when we let grass grow under our feet ?

definitions.text: But not when we let grass grow under our feet ?

parts.words: But not when we let grass grow under our feet
parts.note: occasions of lively outdoor activity spent on grass, the reverse of idling

explanation.definitionFit: Field days are days of busy activity and sport out of doors, far from letting time slip by idly.

clue.text: Right to upset a card-game ? Go back over this

indicators.note: in a down clue the card game's name is turned upside down

parts.note: ecarte is a two-handed card game of French origin

explanation.surface: Someone loses at cards and tries to replay every move.
explanation.walkthrough: Ecarte is a French card game for two; 'upset' suits a down clue, where the word is read from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrace steps or reasoning is to go over the same route again.

clue.text: Solid enough, but with ragged coat, he leads the doctor on

indicators.note: the word he comes before the doctor, at the head
the coat is made ragged, so its letters are torn about

parts.note: taken as written
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tough but scruffy man in a torn coat escorts the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: An octahedron is a three-dimensional solid figure with eight faces.

clue.text: B.B.C. hospitality offered to private broadcaster?

parts.note: the British Broadcasting Corporation was then above all a radio service
cold ham is the classic dish set before a guest

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the BBC lays on a spread for an independent broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: A radio ham is an amateur who transmits from home; the clue pretends the ham is a plate of meat offered by the wireless.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur wireless operator transmits on his own account, a broadcaster in a private capacity.

clue.text: Legendary, this cycle

parts.note: the cycle of legends about the king of Camelot and his knights

explanation.definitionFit: The body of tales about Camelot's king and the Round Table is called a cycle of legend.

clue.text: I had no money for this adorable creature

parts.note: I'd is the short form of I had
O, nought, means no or nothing
L stands for the pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone without a penny gave all they had for a beloved pet.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a figure worshipped or adored, an object of devotion.

clue.text: Miss Prism's unconventional baby-carrier

parts.note: in Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest the governess left the infant in a bag at Victoria station

explanation.definitionFit: In Wilde's comedy the baby was left in a lady's bag in a station cloakroom.

clue.text: Comes across sound sources of protein

indicators.note: the clue says the protein word is heard, matching its pronunciation

parts.note: meats are foods rich in protein

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles on healthy sources of protein.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across someone is to encounter them by chance.

clue.text: Whirlybird, say ?

parts.note: a bird whose name is pronounced like a whirl or spin; whirlybird is also slang for a helicopter

explanation.definitionFit: The tern is a seabird, and its name sounds like a turn, a whirl.

clue.text: Give the right style

definitions.meaning: to grant someone a claim or permission
as a verb, to call by a title or name

explanation.definitionFit: Entitling grants a claim to something, and also bestows a title, which is to style or name someone.

clue.text: Sailor Jack lacks a lightweight to beat

indicators.note: the sailor goes without the letter a, so it is removed from his name

parts.note: Jack Tar is the old nickname for a sailor
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A seaman short of a featherweight boxer cannot win his fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a second sailor or a name, but Jack Tar is one sailor; 'lacks a' takes away the letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to defeat soundly, to thrash an opponent.

clue.text: Has nothing unpaid — difficult, but in the clear

indicators.note: the letters are made awkward, put into a hard tangle

parts.note: O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone who has paid nothing owed is in a tricky spot yet still escapes blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' rearranges HAS + O + UNPAID; 'in the clear' looks like 'free of blame', but 'clear' means transparent.
explanation.definitionFit: Diaphanous fabric is so fine and light that it is see-through, transparent.

clue.text: One brother or sister returns for the bird

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: the word for a sibling comes back, so it reads right to left

parts.note: a sib is a sibling, a brother or a sister

explanation.surface: A sibling comes home to see the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a curved bill, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Good man and quiet makes no move. (It's freezing !)

parts.note: St, saint, is a good man
still means quiet, silent

explanation.surface: A saintly fellow stays perfectly quiet and motionless in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: '(It's freezing!)' adds colour: a standstill is a freeze.
explanation.definitionFit: A standstill is a state with no movement at all.

clue.text: Bill improved, perhaps, but says he's finished

definitions.meaning: a parliamentary bill that has been altered for the better

explanation.surface: A bill has been revised, but its sponsor declares himself finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as AM ENDED: someone who 'says he's finished' says he am-ended.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill gets changed in committee; the second reading is a split into 'am ended', a declaration of being done for.

clue.text: Enjoyed playing — perished without play

indicators.note: in the old sense outside: the word for perished is wrapped outside play

parts.note: died means perished
sport means play

explanation.surface: Someone had fun right up to their death, without any game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking', but here it carries its old sense of 'outside', so play sits inside the word for perished.
explanation.definitionFit: To disport oneself is to amuse oneself, to frolic.

clue.text: A whole number of sheep in Erin, perhaps

indicators.note: the young sheep is put inside the other letters
the letters of the old name for Ireland are taken loosely, perhaps in another order

parts.note: a teg is a sheep in its second year

explanation.surface: Someone wonders about the total number of sheep in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Erin is the poetic name for Ireland, and 'perhaps' signals that its letters are rearranged around the young sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a number with no fractional part, such as 3 or -12.

clue.text: Among others it takes crumbled bread

definitions.text: Among others it takes crumbled bread

indicators.note: the word for others takes in the broken bread

parts.note: the rest means the others

indicators.note: the bread is broken into crumbs, so its letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A garden bird joins the others to peck at breadcrumbs.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and a picture of the robin, the garden bird that takes crumbs from among the others.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin, with its red breast, is famous for taking crumbs from garden tables.

clue.text: Portly polygamists ?

parts.note: people with a wife in every port: 'portly' read as belonging to ports, not stout

explanation.definitionFit: Seafarers are proverbially said to have a wife in every port they visit.

clue.text: Their Summer Time comes after 'ours.

parts.note: a late warm spell in autumn is named after the people of America, and comes after our summer

explanation.definitionFit: An Indian summer is a warm spell late in autumn, after the normal summer.

clue.text: Kind son turned out to keep, one from slipping

indicators.note: the letters are turned out of their order and set out anew

explanation.surface: A kind boy grows up to stop someone from falling.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-skid tyre or surface grips and prevents sliding.

clue.text: They took a lot of trouble for Tommy -

definitions.text: They took a lot of trouble for Tommy -

parts.words: They took a lot of trouble for Tommy
parts.note: the soldiers' song 'Pack up your troubles in your old kit-bag'; Tommy is the British private soldier

explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers' bags for gear were where the First World War song told Tommies to pack their troubles.

clue.text: Stuffy lodgings ?

parts.note: lodgings, in slang, that are also stuffed cushions

explanation.definitionFit: A pad is slang for a flat or digs, and also a cushion stuffed with padding.

clue.text: Catches poached from Peter, say?

indicators.note: say marks that it is the pronunciation that counts

parts.note: in 'rob Peter to pay Paul' what is taken from Peter belongs to Paul

explanation.surface: Fish caught by poaching from a man called Peter.
explanation.walkthrough: From the proverb 'rob Peter to pay Paul': what is poached from Peter is Paul's.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawl is a pivoted bar that catches the teeth of a ratchet.

clue.text: The last man to set the crossword

definitions.text: The last man to set the crossword

parts.words: The last man to set the crossword
parts.note: the clue sounds like the setter, but means the printer who sets the puzzle in type, the final hand before print

explanation.definitionFit: A typesetter arranges type for printing, so he sets the puzzle after its author.

clue.text: Hamlet's detective thing

parts.note: Hamlet says 'the ...'s the thing wherein I'll catch the conscience of the king', a drama staged to expose a murderer

explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet stages a drama to detect the king's guilt, calling it 'the thing'.

clue.text: Yield-what began it, we hear

indicators.note: the words are spoken, so their sound is what is entered

parts.note: a seed is the origin from which something grows

explanation.surface: A plea to give way, since what started the trouble is known by rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to give up or surrender ground or a right.

clue.text: Not the most hardy wallflower ?

parts.note: a hardy plant is one that survives cold; the least hardy flower is the feeblest, and a wallflower is also a shy, timid person

explanation.definitionFit: The least hardy is the feeblest; the superlative of feeble is the same idea.

clue.text: It was made hot for his enemies when they jarred on him

definitions.text: It was made hot for his enemies when they jarred on him

parts.words: It was made hot for his enemies when they jarred on him
parts.note: the robbers who hid in oil jars to ambush the hero were scalded by boiling oil

explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale, the forty thieves hid in jars and were killed with boiling oil poured in.

clue.text: It all hangs on what America pays out

definitions.text: It all hangs on what America pays out

parts.words: It all hangs on what America pays out
parts.note: a word meaning hangs that, split up, suggests the United States spending money

explanation.walkthrough: The verb means 'hangs' or 'holds up'; the rest plays on US and SPENDS within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend is to hang something up, or to defer it pending a decision.

clue.text: Little room near the leader

parts.note: close means near

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word 'the' is taken

explanation.surface: A small room sits right beside the chief's office.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet is a small private chamber or cupboard.
